bills.title: Expressing support for the designation of the first week of August as "National Community Health Center Week", and encouraging all Americans to participate by visiting their local community health center and celebrating the important partnership between health centers and the communities they serve.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
bills.nexus: This resolution has no discernible nexus to Treasury's statutory authorities, appropriations, or regulatory responsibilities. No action or briefing by Treasury's Legislative Affairs team is warranted.

bills.title: Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and Treasury Data Access Act
bills.nexus: H.R. 8463 directly implicates the Bureau of the Fiscal Service and the Do Not Pay Business Center, which operate under Treasury's authority to verify payment eligibility and prevent improper disbursements government-wide. Treasury must assess implementation demands on its data-matching infrastructure and any expanded interagency data-sharing obligations that could create compliance, privacy, or operational risk.

bills.title: PRIMATE Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: The PRIMATE Act's referral to Ways and Means signals potential tariff or trade-remedy provisions that would fall under Treasury's Office of Tax Policy or Customs revenue authorities. Treasury would monitor implementation risk around any import restrictions or duty adjustments affecting primate-related goods or research materials crossing U.S. borders.

bills.title: Working Americans’ Tax Cut Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7937 directly implicates IRS and the Office of Tax Policy, as any statutory change to individual income tax rates or credits requires Treasury to issue guidance, update withholding tables, and revise forms. The implementation risk centers on administrative lead time and revenue scoring, since a rate cut affecting working taxpayers carries significant baseline cost implications that Treasury's Office of Tax Analysis must model for budget purposes.

bills.title: Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026
bills.status: Read the second time. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 347.
bills.nexus: S. 3977 adjusts the debt eligibility thresholds for small-business and individual bankruptcy filings under Subchapter V of the Bankruptcy Code, directly implicating Treasury's Office of Financial Research and its monitoring of financial system stress and credit market stability. Treasury should track this bill because threshold changes affect the volume and composition of distressed-debt resolutions, carrying downstream risk implications for federally backed lending programs and financial institution exposure data.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to establish a credit for adult child caregivers.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 7610 amends the Internal Revenue Code, directly implicating IRS's authority under Treasury to design and administer a new individual tax credit. Treasury faces implementation risk in defining eligible "adult child caregiver" relationships, setting income or expense thresholds, and building compliance and verification infrastructure before any effective date.

bills.title: Airborne Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus:
Without a known nexus provided, I'll flag the most likely Treasury angle based on the bill's committee referral.

H.R. 7460 is before Ways and Means, meaning any tax provisions or revenue offsets it contains fall within IRS and Office of Tax Policy jurisdiction. Treasury's risk is that new aviation-related tax expenditures or excise modifications could affect the Airport and Airway Trust Fund baseline and require IRS regulatory guidance to implement.

bills.title: Retirement Simplification and Clarity Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 6324 falls within Treasury's purview because the IRS, operating under Treasury authority, administers the tax-qualification rules and required minimum distribution regulations governing retirement plans that the bill would modify. Treasury and IRS would bear the implementation burden of issuing updated guidance, redesigning compliance procedures, and absorbing any revenue impact from rule changes affecting tax-deferred retirement savings.

bills.title: Gun Safety Incentive Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: H.R. 4487 is referred to Ways and Means because it likely uses the tax code (such as excise taxes or credits) to create financial incentives tied to gun safety measures, directly implicating Treasury/IRS authority over tax administration. Treasury's implementation risk centers on designing and enforcing any new tax incentive structure, including eligibility determinations, compliance verification, and potential revenue impact.

bills.title: Tax Relief for Victims of Crimes, Scams, and Disasters Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 3469 directly implicates the Internal Revenue Service and the Office of Tax Policy, as it would modify the Internal Revenue Code to expand exclusions or deductions for losses suffered by crime, fraud, and disaster victims. Treasury faces implementation risk in defining qualifying events, administering verification of claims, and estimating the revenue cost of broadened loss provisions.

bills.title: Roberto Clemente Commemorative Coin Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 1787 directs the Secretary of the Treasury to mint and issue commemorative coins honoring Roberto Clemente, engaging the U.S. Mint under Treasury's Bureau authority and requiring appropriation of surcharge proceeds to a designated beneficiary. Treasury bears the implementation burden of coin design approval, production cost recovery, and ensuring surcharge disbursement complies with the commemorative coin program's statutory framework.

bills.title: Fair Access to Banking Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: The Fair Access to Banking Act would direct the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to require large national banks to make credit and banking services available on a quantitative, risk-based basis rather than on reputational or political grounds, directly implicating OCC's chartering and supervisory authority. Treasury cares because finalizing or defending a fair-access rule carries significant implementation complexity and litigation risk, and the bill could constrain how OCC-supervised institutions manage reputational and portfolio-level risk across politically sensitive industries.

bills.title: American CANS Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 914, the American CANS Act, falls within Treasury's purview because the Ways and Means referral signals potential changes to tax-related provisions that the Internal Revenue Service, under Treasury's authority, would be responsible for administering. Treasury's implementation risk centers on any new compliance requirements, revenue scoring impacts, or regulatory guidance IRS would need to issue if the bill advances.

bills.title: Hearing Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
bills.nexus: The Hearing Protection Act would remove suppressors from regulation under the National Firearms Act, directly affecting the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives tax collection authority administered through Treasury's legacy NFA framework and the $200 transfer tax currently remitted to IRS. Treasury faces both revenue loss risk from elimination of that excise tax and administrative transition risk if ATF's NFA registry and tax-stamp processing infrastructure must be restructured.
